children: Poland's central bank said on Thursday its gold reserves had reached 648 metric tons, implying purchases of 7.8 tons in August, matching the amount bought in July.

National Bank of Poland (NBP) Governor Adam Glapinski told a press conference following NBP's interest rate decision that the central bank was on track to increase its gold reserves to 700 tons, making "purchases when the opportunity is right."

The 700-ton target is a "volume that truly provides us with stability - stability for the zloty, for our ratings, and for the credibility of our payments and solvency - absolute stability, even though we border a country where a massive war is raging," Glapinski said, referring to Russia's war in Ukraine.
Poland has been the largest buyer of gold among central banks reporting their purchases so far this year, according to World Gold Council data.
The pace of the Polish central bank's monthly buying in July and August was the slowest since December, according to World Gold Council data.

Poland's annual gold purchases for the reserves averaged 107 tons a year in 2023-2025. By the end of July, the country had already added 90 tons this year, putting 2026 on track to match the levels seen in recent years, consultancy Metals Focus said in a note.
